verdicts.reasoning: The toggle is an <input type="checkbox"> with role="switch" added. The API reference lists no Switch component, so the diff does not use a design-system switch control. It relies on a native checkbox with an ARIA role override, which is a checkbox underneath and does not clearly meet the 'system's on/off switch control, not checkboxes' requirement.

Each setting has a title (a <label> with the setting name) and a supporting description (a <span> linked via aria-describedby), which matches the general title-plus-description shape. However, the diff does not show or reuse any system settings-row component or pattern, so conformance to 'the system's settings-row pattern' cannot be verified from the diff. The row is hand-assembled from Stack, label, and span.

The section is built from the system's layout primitives: Surface wraps the content, and Stack with gap tokens (space.5, space.4, space.1) handles the vertical and horizontal grouping and spacing of the header, rows, and text pair. No ad-hoc margins or padding values are used for spacing. Minor deduction because the heading uses an inline style for margin and colour rather than a primitive.
